text:
nicole_sales: urgent: Prospect (DataBridge) just hit 413 during a live POC. They POSTed one big JSON with 18 PDFs embedded (base64) and the assistant response was truncated. Demo in 40m, need a quick customer-safe fix.

ethan_se: 413 = gateway/proxy limit. We default to client_max_body_size ~4MB. Base64 in JSON will bloat payload ~33% on top of original.

marta_support: Fastest fixes (in order):
1) Client-side gzip the combined text and set Content-Encoding: gzip (gateway accepts compressed bodies).
2) Presign + upload then POST an /ingest with the key so we fetch server-side.
3) Switch to embed+retrieval so generate requests only include top-k passages.

nicole_sales: They insist on a single HTTP call for the demo. Will gzip keep it simple?

ethan_se: Yes — gzip is the lowest friction. But warning: compression only helps transport; tokens are charged after decompression, so cost remains. Also they must NOT base64 files in JSON if they gzip. Send raw text or binary.

marta_support: Minimal gzip curl they can run now (one-liner):
```
echo -n "$(cat combined_text.txt)" | gzip -c | curl -s -X POST \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' \
  -H 'Content-Encoding: gzip' \
  --data-binary @- 'https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate?model=rwd-4x&max_tokens=1200'
```
Add to message: "Do not base64 inside JSON; that will still blow up size."

lee_oncall: Note on retries: the prospect retried immediately after a 413 and then got 429s. 413 indicates client-side fix required  don't auto-retry on 413. For 429 implement exponential backoff and respect Retry-After header.

icole_sales: If gzip doesn't work can eng temporarily raise the proxy limit for the demo IP?

lee_oncall: We can do a short exception. I'll open a ticket to increase client_max_body_size to 50MB for that IP for 60 minutes and request SOC approval. Ping infra_bot.

infra_bot: ticket-13077 opened: "Demo body-size exception for IP 203.0.113.101". Requested change: proxy client_max_body_size=50MB for 60m. SOC approval pending. ETA ~20m.

marta_support: If the customer prefers presign flow (single UX with invisible server fetch) send them these steps:
1) POST /presign -> returns upload_url and key
2) Client PUTs file to upload_url
3) POST /ingest {"source_key":"<key>","model":"rwd-4x","max_tokens":1200} -> we fetch and run generate
Example cURL chain (minimal):
```
# 1) get presign
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/presign -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"filename":"bundle.zip"}'
# 2) client uploads
curl -X PUT "<upload_url>" --upload-file bundle.zip
# 3) notify ingest
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/ingest -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"source_key":"<s3_key>","model":"rwd-4x"}'
```

ethan_se: Longer-term: show them an embed+retrieval POC. Precompute embeddings for their docs, store vectors in a demo store, and send only the retrieved passages in the generate call. Much lower tokens and predictable latency/cost. We can provide a small sample app.

icole_sales: Please DM the gzip curl and the presign steps to the prospect now. Also open the whitelist ticket; I'll tell them to try gzip first. Session id: DB-POC-77.

lee_oncall: ticket-13077 submitted for SOC. If approved we'll apply the change and notify here so you can retry the original flow. After the demo we'll revert and run an audit.

marta_support: Quick reminder text to include in the support DM: "If you get 413, do not retry immediately. Try gzip or presign workflow. Compression reduces network size but not token billing; consider trimming docs or using retrieval for cost control."

icole_sales: thanks all  sending now. Will update after the demo. :thumbsup:
